extracted.intended_audience: journal editors, publishers, editorial boards, peer reviewers, and researchers involved in scholarly publishing
extracted.subtask_description: A collection of COPE guidelines covering publication ethics and journal management topics (retractions, consent for case reports, text recycling, peer-review ethics, cooperation with institutions, etc.) intended to guide editors and publishers in ethical decision-making and policy-setting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidelines for managing the relationships between society owned journals, their society, and publishers
rubrics_metrics.description: The journals of ‘Learned Societies’ and ‘Professional Associations’ are an important part of the scientific literature. Regardless of the publication arrangements (ie, self-published by the society, published under contract with a professional publishing house, or some combination of both) and the number of journals affiliated with that society, the policies of and the relationships among the j…
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addresses the complex relationships among societies, their journals, and publishers and the need for clear, ethically sound policies and management arrangements. (Full guidance available in the linked document.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Principles of Transparency and Best Practice in Scholarly Publishing
rubrics_metrics.description: Principles developed jointly by COPE, DOAJ, OASPA, and WAME setting out transparency and best-practice standards for scholarly publishing (Version 3, January 2018).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A consolidated set of principles for transparency and best practice in publishing (publisher/journal disclosure, editorial policies, peer review description, ownership, revenue sources, advertising policies, etc.). Specific points are provided in the full document.

rubrics_metrics.name: Journals’ Best Practices for ensuring consent for publishing medical case reports
rubrics_metrics.description: The publication of case reports is a common practice in medical journals... they pose a specific ethical challenge for journals because, by their ve…
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasises that case reports raise particular ethical issues around patient consent and identifiability; journals should adopt clear procedures to ensure informed consent for publication (see full guidance for practical requirements and examples).

rubrics_metrics.name: Sharing of information among editors-in-chief regarding possible misconduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance drafted following a COPE Discussion Forum (4 September 2013) on sharing of information among editors-in-chief regarding possible misconduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers how editors may communicate about allegations of misconduct, including relevant considerations around allegations, complaints and appeals, and conflicts of interest; provides procedures and principles for information-sharing among editors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Text recycling guidelines for editors
rubrics_metrics.description: A common issue encountered by editors is overlap of text with an author’s own previously published work, particularly with the increasing use of plagiarism detection software. This practice is known as ‘text recycling’ (also sometimes referred to as ‘self-plagiarism’). Opinions on the acceptability of text recycling vary greatly and it can be a challenge for editors to know how to deal with it…
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains the phenomenon of text recycling, notes the impact of plagiarism-detection tools, and offers editorial approaches for evaluating overlap, distinguishing acceptable reuse from problematic self-plagiarism, and communicating policies to authors.

rubrics_metrics.name: A short guide to ethical editing for new editors
rubrics_metrics.description: This short guide aims to summarise key issues and to provide links to relevant pages of the COPE website as well as those of other organisations. 1. Initial assessment of journal wh…
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides practical advice for new editors, including initial assessments of the journal, key ethical considerations, structures and processes to put in place, and links to more detailed COPE guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cooperation between research institutions and journals on research integrity cases
rubrics_metrics.description: Institutions and journals both have important duties relating to research and publication misconduct. Institutions are responsible for the conduct of their researchers and for encouraging a healthy research environment. Journals are responsible for the conduct of their editors, for safeguarding the research record, and for ensuring the reliability of everything t…
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines complementary responsibilities of institutions and journals in handling integrity cases and offers guidance on communication, investigation roles, and processes to resolve allegations while protecting the research record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidelines for the Board of Directors of Learned Society Journals
rubrics_metrics.description: The journals of Learned Societies are an important part of the scientific literature. Their management should be of the highest quality and ethically sound.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advises boards on governance, the complex relationship between editors and societies, and expectations for ethical management and oversight of society-owned journals.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to handle authorship disputes: a guide for new researchers
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the main tasks of COPE’s education committee is to reduce unethical behaviour. This involves the rather bold step of defining when people have been behaving unethically, and then providing suggestions on how they can avoid doing so in the future. To this end we have written, and tested on a group of authors, a guide for young researchers on the area of authorship, which many people agree…
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines unethical behaviours related to authorship and offers practical suggestions and processes for resolving disputes and avoiding unethical authorship practices (see full guide for procedures and examples).

rubrics_metrics.name: Retraction guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors should consider retracting a publication if: They have clear evidence that the findings are unreliable, either as a result of major error (eg, miscalculation or experimental error), or as a result of fabrication (eg, of data) or falsification (eg, image manipulation) It constitutes plagiarism The findings have previously been published el…
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lists reasons for retraction including unreliable findings due to major error, fabrication or falsification, plagiarism, and duplicate publication; provides editorial procedures for issuing retractions and safeguarding the integrity of the literature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical guidelines for peer reviewers (English)
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer review in all its forms plays an important role in ensuring the integrity of the scholarly record. The process depends to a large extent on trust, and requires that everyone involved behaves responsibly and ethically. Peer reviewers play a central and critical part in the peer-review process, but too often come to the role without any guidance and unaware of their ethical obligations. COPE…
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets out ethical obligations and expected behaviours for peer reviewers (confidentiality, objectivity, declaration of conflicts, timeliness, constructive feedback). The page introduces the guidance; full document contains detailed principles and examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidance for Editors: research, audit and service evaluations
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulations regarding what type of study requires ethical approval vary worldwide. In some countries all studies require ethical approval but in others not. This may lead to submission to journals of manuscripts relating to such studies that do not satisfy the journal’s normal requirement for independent ethical approval, and rejection of the manuscript because of misunderstanding of local regu…
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains variability in ethical approval requirements across jurisdictions and provides advice for editors on assessing whether submitted research, audits, or service evaluations require ethical approval and how to handle submissions lacking clear approval.
